It starts with a short, time-boxed documentation phase (design brief, content inventory, wireframes, tokens, motion spec, architecture) because no code is written until the big decisions have written answers. A deployed, themed, budgeted skeleton then proves hosting, CI, theming and reduced-motion handling before anything is built on top. Next comes a content-complete site with navigation, resume and copy-email, so the recruiter fast path works before any motion is layered on. The motion system and the signature project rail (reference 539: hover/lift on desktop, swipe and tap on touch, focused overlay) come after that. The rail is the first real use of the animation layer, and the phase ends with measured keep-or-drop decisions on react-spring and LazyMotion. Section treatments (experience cards, skills slider, education card, hero text effect) follow. Real-device hardening and the additive cutover into `aa-phan.github.io` come last, so the v1 iPod site stays live and rollback stays trivial until the new site has passed every gate.\n6\t\n7\t## Phases\n8\t\n9\t**Phase Numbering:**\n10\t\n11\t- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work\n12\t- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)\n13\t\n14\tDecimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.\n15\t\n16\t- [x] **Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation** - Time-boxed design, content, IA, tokens, motion and architecture docs that gate all code (completed 2026-10-09)\n17\t- [x] **Phase 2: Deployed Themed Skeleton** - Vite/React/TS/Tailwind app live on the project URL with CI, JS budget, light/dark tokens and one motion-preference source (completed 2026-10-26)\n18\t- [ ] **Phase 3: Content-Complete Site** - All six sections with real content, resume download, copy-email and navigation, passing the 10-second phone test\n19\t- [ ] **Phase 4: Motion System and Signature Rail** - Shared motion rules plus the handled-object project rail with overlay, touch and keyboard paths\n20\t- [ ] **Phase 5: Section Treatments** - Expandable experience cards, skills slider, education card and hero text effect\n21\t- [ ] **Phase 6: Hardening and Cutover** - Lighthouse, real-device, keyboard/VoiceOver/axe gates, launch assets, and the additive cutover with a written rollback\n22\t\n23\t## Phase Details\n24\t\n25\t### Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation\n26\t\n27\t**Goal:** As a site owner, I want to have time-boxed design, content, motion and architecture docs, so that every major decision is settled before any code is written.\n28\t**Mode:** mvp\n29\t**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)\n30\t**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-05, DOC-06, CNT-03\n31\t**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):\n32\t\n33\t  1. It starts with a short, time-boxed documentation phase (design brief, content inventory, wireframes, tokens, motion spec, architecture) because no code is written until the big decisions have written answers. A deployed, themed, budgeted skeleton then proves hosting, CI, theming and reduced-motion handling before anything is built on top. Next comes a content-complete site with navigation, resume and copy-email, so the recruiter fast path works before any motion is layered on. The motion system and the signature project rail (reference 539: hover/lift on desktop, swipe and tap on touch, focused overlay) come after that. The rail is the first real use of the animation layer, and the phase ends with measured keep-or-drop decisions on react-spring and LazyMotion. Section treatments (experience cards, skills slider, education card, hero text effect) follow. Content schema | Types for all content | `src/content/schema.ts` |\n87\t| Content aggregate | Single `siteContent` object | `src/content/index.ts` |\n88\t\n89\t## Pattern Overview\n90\t\n91\t**Overall:** Single-page React application with a static content layer, a single page composition root, and an enforced animation boundary. No router, no server, no store library.\n92\t\n93\t**Key Characteristics:**\n94\t- One route. `index.html` plus `404.html` are the only HTML entries. `404.html` is a second Rollup input (`vite.config.ts`) that GitHub Pages serves for unknown paths.\n95\t- Content is typed TypeScript data, not a CMS or fetched JSON. Everything is bundled at build time.\n96\t- Animation is isolated behind `src/anim/`. Components do not import motion libraries directly.\n97\t- Theme state lives in the DOM attribute `html[data-theme]`, which is the single source of truth. `localStorage` persists an explicit choice.\n98\t- The motion feature bundle (`domMax`) is split into its own chunk via `src/anim/features.ts` and loaded after first paint.\n99\t- Section lazy-loading: `src/anim/declarative/TextReveal.tsx` lazy-loads `motion-primitives/text-effect` with `React.lazy` and `Suspense`.\n100\t\n101\t## Layers\n102\t\n103\t**Entry and composition:**\n104\t- Purpose: Mount the app and compose sections in order\n105\t- Location: `src/main.tsx`, `src/app/`\n106\t- Contains: `App.tsx`, `Providers.tsx`, `Page.tsx`\n107\t- Depends on: `src/content`, `src/layout`, `src/sections`, `src/anim`, `src/components/ui`, `src/hooks`\n108\t- Used by: Nothing (root)\n109\t\n110\t**Layout:**\n111\t- Purpose: Persistent chrome around sections\n112\t- Location: `src/layout/`\n113\t- Contains: header, pill nav, footer, container, section wrapper, skip link, wordmark, nav item definitions\n114\t- Depends on: `src/anim` (through barrel), `src/hooks`, `src/components/ui`, `src/lib`\n115\t- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`\n116\t\n117\t**Sections:**\n118\t- Purpose: Page content blocks\n119\t- Location: `src/sections/<Name>/`\n120\t- Contains: presentational components taking typed props (`profile`, `entries`, `groups`, `links`, `email`)\n121\t- Depends on: `src/anim` barrel, `src/layout/*`, `src/components/ui`, `src/lib`, `src/content/images` for images, and `src/content/schema` types\n122\t- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`\n123\t\n124\t**Shared UI and hooks:**\n125\t- Purpose: Reusable controls, icons, toast, theme, scroll-spy\n126\t- Location: `src/components/ui/`, `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/`\n127\t- Contains: `CtaLink.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `Toast.tsx`, icon components in `src/components/ui/icons/`, `useActiveSection.ts`, `useTheme.ts`, `theme.ts`, `copy.ts`, `utils.ts`\n128\t- Depends on: React, browser APIs\n129\t- Used by: layout, sections, app\n130\t\n131\t**Animation:**\n132\t- Purpose: All motion behavior, reduced-motion handling, lazy motion features\n133\t- Location: `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/`\n134\t- Contains: barrel `index.ts`, declarative and physics components, preference provider, token file\n135\t- Depends on: `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`\n136\t- Used by: layout, sections, app providers. Only through the `@/anim` barrel.\n137\t\n138\t**Content:**\n139\t- Purpose: Site copy and structured data\n140\t- Location: `src/content/`\n141\t- Contains: `profile.ts`, `contacts.ts`, `experience.ts`, `projects.ts`, `skills.ts`, `education.ts`, `schema.ts`, `images.ts`, `index.ts`\n142\t- Depends on: `src/assets/images/*` (through `images.ts`)\n143\t- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx` only (enforced by lint)\n144\t\n145\t**Styles:**\n146\t- Purpose: Design tokens and global CSS\n147\t- Location: `src/styles/`\n148\t- Contains: `index.css` (entry, imports the others), `tokens.css`, `base.css`, `interactions.css`, `not-found.css`\n149\t- Used by: `src/main.tsx` imports `./styles/index.css`\n150\t\n151\t## Data Flow\n152\t\n153\t### Primary Request Path (page load)\n154\t\n155\t1. Browser loads `index.html`; the inline script sets `html[data-theme]` from `localStorage` or the OS scheme before first paint (`index.html`)\n156\t2. Vite-built module `src/main.tsx` imports the font and CSS, then renders `<App />` into `#root` (`src/main.tsx`)\n157\t3. `App` wraps `Page` in `Providers` (`src/app/App.tsx`, `src/app/Providers.tsx`)\n158\t4. `Page` reads `siteContent` from `src/content/index.ts`, extracts the `email` link and the remaining contact links (`src/app/Page.tsx`)\n159\t5. `Page` calls `useActiveSection(SECTION_IDS)` (`src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`) and passes `activeId` and `lockTo` to `SiteHeader` and `PillNav`\n160\t6. Sections render with typed props. Images resolve to imagetools output via `src/content/images.ts`\n161\t\n162\t### Theme Toggle Path\n163\t\n164\t1. `ThemeToggle` calls `applyTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts`\n165\t2. The attribute `data-theme` is written first, then `localStorage` (`THEME_STORAGE_KEY`)\n166\t3. `subscribeTheme` observes the attribute with a `MutationObserver`, and reacts to `storage` events and OS `prefers-color-scheme` changes when nothing is stored\n167\t4. `src/hooks/useTheme.ts` exposes the value to React\n168\t\n169\t### Section Navigation Path\n170\t\n171\t1. Desktop `SiteHeader` and mobile `PillNav` call `onNavigate` = `lockTo(id)` (`src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`)\n172\t2. `lockTo` sets `activeId` immediately and suppresses the observer until `scrollend`, a quiet period, a fallback timer, or a cap timer releases it\n173\t3. The single `IntersectionObserver` band (`rootMargin` built from `--nav-h` and `-60%` bottom) updates `activeId` otherwise\n174\t\n175\t### Copy Email Path\n176\t\n177\t1. Hero and Contact call `useCopyEmail` (`src/components/ui/useCopyEmail.ts`)\n178\t2. `copyText` in `src/lib/copy.ts` tries `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, then falls back to a hidden textarea with `document.execCommand('copy')`\n179\t3. Result is announced through a live region and a toast (`src/components/ui/useToast.ts`, `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`)\n180\t\n181\t**State Management:**\n182\t- No global store. State is local to hooks and components, plus React context for motion preference and toasts.\n183\t- Theme truth is the DOM attribute, not React state. React reads it through `readTheme()`.\n184\t- Scroll-spy state is a `useState` plus refs (`prevRef`, `intersectingRef`, `lockedRef`, `releaseLockRef`, `recomputeRef`) inside `useActiveSection`.\n185\t\n186\t## Key Abstractions\n187\t\n188\t**`siteContent` aggregate:**\n189\t- Purpose: One typed object holding all site data\n190\t- Examples: `src/content/index.ts`\n191\t- Pattern: Plain `export const` data, typed by `src/content/schema.ts`. `contacts.ts` uses `as const satisfies readonly ContactLink[]`.\n192\t\n193\t**Animation barrel:**\n194\t- Purpose: Stable public API for animation, the only allowed import path\n195\t- Examples: `src/anim/index.ts` (exports `MotionFeatures`, `MotionPreferenceProvider`, `ThemeThumb`, and others)\n196\t- Pattern: Facade. Consumers import `@/anim`, never `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n197\t\n198\t**Vendored primitives:**\n199\t- Purpose: Copy-in source from motion-primitives, owned by this repo\n200\t- Examples: `src/components/motion-primitives/text-effect.tsx`\n201\t- Pattern: Source ownership. Edited in place, not installed from npm. Lint rules are turned off for this directory (`.oxlintrc.json` override).\n202\t\n203\t**Scroll-spy hook:**\n204\t- Purpose: Determine the active section and manage click-lock\n205\t- Examples: `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts` (pure helper `pickActive` is exported for unit tests in `tests/unit/active-section.test.ts`)\n206\t- Pattern: IntersectionObserver with a computed band, plus timers for lock release\n207\t\n208\t**Toast and copy:**\n209\t- Purpose: Transient feedback after copying the email\n210\t- Examples: `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`, `src/components/ui/useToast.ts`, `src/components/ui/useCopyEmail.ts`, `src/lib/copy.ts`\n211\t- Pattern: Context provider plus a hook. Live region for screen readers.\n212\t\n213\t**Project dialog:**\n214\t- Purpose: Project detail view\n215\t- Examples: `src/sections/Projects/ProjectDialog.tsx`\n216\t- Pattern: Native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` called in an effect (ADR-0006 native path, referenced in the file's comments)\n217\t\n218\t## Entry Points\n219\t\n220\t**Application:**\n221\t- Location: `src/main.tsx`\n222\t- Triggers: Browser loads `index.html` (dev server or built `dist/index.html`)\n223\t- Responsibilities: Font import, global CSS import, root render in `StrictMode`\n224\t\n225\t**Not-found page:**\n226\t- Location: `404.html` (second Rollup input in `vite.config.ts`). Styled by `src/styles/not-found.css`.\n227\t- Triggers: GitHub Pages serves it for unknown paths\n228\t- Responsibilities: Static fallback page\n229\t\n230\t**Build and check entries:**\n231\t- Location: `vite.config.ts`, `scripts/*.mjs`\n232\t- Triggers: `npm run build`, `npm run verify`, CI workflows\n233\t- Responsibilities: bundling, asset checks, budget and policy checks\n234\t\n235\t## Architectural Constraints\n236\t\n237\t- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser main thread. No Web Workers in `src/`.\n238\t- **Global state:** `src/lib/theme.ts` holds a module-level `unsavedChoice` flag. `html[data-theme]` is global DOM state. `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts` holds scroll and timer state per hook instance.\n239\t- **Circular imports:** None observed during exploration.\n240\t- **Import boundaries (enforced by oxlint `no-restricted-imports` in `.oxlintrc.json`):**\n241\t  - `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`, `framer-motion`, `motion`, `react-spring` are allowed only in `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/`\n242\t  - Animation must be imported through `@/anim` barrel only\n243\t  - `src/content` may be imported only by `src/app/Page.tsx`\n244\t  - `src/anim/**` must not import `@/sections`, `@/layout`, or `@/content`\n245\t  - `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` checks these rules against fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`\n246\t- **Reduced motion:** Honored through `src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts` and `MotionPreferenceProvider`. Respect this in any new animation.\n247\t- **Static output only:** No runtime server. Any dynamic behavior must run in the browser.\n248\t- **Base path:** Asset URLs must go through `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` or Vite imports, because `VITE_BASE` changes the base.\n249\t\n250\t## Anti-Patterns\n251\t\n252\t### Importing motion libraries directly in a section or layout component\n253\t\n254\t**What happens:** A component imports from `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n255\t**Why it's wrong:** Lint fails (`no-restricted-imports`), and the `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` contract breaks. It also bypasses the lazy feature bundle and reduced-motion handling.\n256\t**Do this instead:** Import from `@/anim` (`src/anim/index.ts`). Add a new export to the barrel if a new primitive is needed.\n257\t\n258\t### Importing content from components\n259\t\n260\t**What happens:** A section or layout file imports `@/content` or `src/content/*` directly to read data.\n261\t**Why it's wrong:** Lint restricts content imports to `src/app/Page.tsx`. Data flow goes top-down from `Page`.\n262\t**Do this instead:** Read data in `src/app/Page.tsx` and pass it as typed props, as `Hero`, `Experience`, `Projects`, and others already do.\n263\t\n264\t### Writing theme state into React state only\n265\t\n266\t**What happens:** Setting theme in component state without writing `html[data-theme]`.\n267\t**Why it's wrong:** The inline bootstrap in `index.html` and `subscribeTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts` both treat the DOM attribute as the source of truth. The two can diverge.\n268\t**Do this instead:** Call `applyTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts` and read with `readTheme`.\n269\t\n270\t### Importing `@/anim/features` statically\n271\t\n272\t**What happens:** A file imports `src/anim/features.ts` directly, pulling `domMax` into the initial graph.\n273\t**Why it's wrong:** The file exists to keep the motion feature bundle in its own chunk, loaded after first paint (`src/anim/features.ts` header comment).\n274\t**Do this instead:** Use `MotionFeatures` from `src/anim/MotionFeatures.tsx`, which loads the feature bundle through `LazyMotion`.\n275\t\n276\t## Error Handling\n277\t\n278\t**Strategy:** Defensive try/catch around browser APIs that can be blocked or missing. Degrade quietly rather than throw.\n279\t\n280\t**Patterns:**\n281\t- `localStorage` access wrapped in try/catch in `src/lib/theme.ts` and `index.html`. The in-memory choice still applies when storage is blocked.\n282\t- `matchMedia` wrapped in try/catch in `src/lib/theme.ts`. Falls back to `light`.\n283\t- Clipboard write falls back from `navigator.clipboard.writeText` to `document.execCommand('copy')` in `src/lib/copy.ts`.\n284\t- `useActiveSection` does nothing when `IntersectionObserver` is missing. `activeId` stays `null`.\n285\t- Scroll lock has fallback and cap timers so a stuck scroll cannot freeze the indicator.\n286\t- `TextReveal` wraps a lazy import in an error boundary class component (`src/anim/declarative/TextReveal.tsx`).\n287\t\n288\t## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n289\t\n290\t**Logging:** None. No logging library. Console output is not a designed channel.\n291\t**Validation:** Compile-time only, via TypeScript types in `src/content/schema.ts` and `satisfies` checks. No runtime validation library.\n292\t**Authentication:** Not applicable (public static site).\n293\t**Accessibility:** Skip link (`src/layout/SkipLink.tsx`), `aria-labelledby` on sections, live region for copy feedback, `prefers-reduced-motion` honored, tests use `axe-core`.\n294\t**Build-time checks:** `scripts/check-*.mjs` enforce path case, color tokens, contrast pairs, JS budget, absence of phone numbers, and image outputs. These run in `npm run verify`.\n295\t\n296\t---\n297\t\n298\t*Architecture analysis: 2026-11-19*\n299\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ea797a68-215d-475b-bda6-167d558fceef","uuid":"a7257abe-696e-4398-b1a8-76baee34b2b6","timestamp":"2026-11-20T03:08:45.568Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/private/var/folders/hl/ryh6jjw90v5gj8hg9j9clckm0000gn/T/avarice-eval-XEEEgF/T01-C-KgYgvN/arm/work/onb_01M7VEJ9Z3TQVY6D9578GZQK7Z/staging/.avarice-knowledge/.planning/codebase/ARCHITECTURE.md","content":"---\nlast_mapped_commit: theme, scroll-spy\n- Location: `src/components/ui/`, `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/`\n- Contains: `CtaLink.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `Toast.tsx`, icon components in `src/components/ui/icons/`, `useActiveSection.ts`, `useTheme.ts`, `theme.ts`, `copy.ts`, `utils.ts`\n- Depends on: React, browser APIs\n- Used by: layout, sections, app\n\n**Animation:**\n- Purpose: All motion behavior, reduced-motion handling, lazy motion features\n- Location: `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/`\n- Contains: barrel `index.ts`, declarative and physics components, preference provider, token file\n- Depends on: `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`\n- Used by: layout, sections, app providers. Only through the `@/anim` barrel.\n\n**Content:**\n- Purpose: Site copy and structured data\n- Location: `src/content/`\n- Contains: `profile.ts`, `contacts.ts`, `experience.ts`, `projects.ts`, `skills.ts`, `education.ts`, `schema.ts`, `images.ts`, `index.ts`\n- Depends on: `src/assets/images/*` (through `images.ts`)\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx` only (enforced by lint)\n\n**Styles:**\n- Purpose: Design tokens and global CSS\n- Location: `src/styles/`\n- Contains: `index.css` (entry, imports the others), `tokens.css`, `base.css`, `interactions.css`, `not-found.css`\n- Used by: `src/main.tsx` imports `./styles/index.css`\n\n## Data Flow\n\n### Primary Request Path (page load)\n\n1. Browser loads `index.html`; the inline script sets `html[data-theme]` from `localStorage` or the OS scheme before first paint (`index.html`)\n2. Vite-built module `src/main.tsx` imports the font and CSS, then renders `<App />` into `#root` (`src/main.tsx`)\n3. `App` wraps `Page` in `Providers` (`src/app/App.tsx`, `src/app/Providers.tsx`)\n4. `Page` reads `siteContent` from `src/content/index.ts`, extracts the `email` link and the remaining contact links (`src/app/Page.tsx`)\n5. `Page` calls `useActiveSection(SECTION_IDS)` (`src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`) and passes `activeId` and `lockTo` to `SiteHeader` and `PillNav`\n6. Sections render with typed props. Images resolve to imagetools output via `src/content/images.ts`\n\n### Theme Toggle Path\n\n1. `ThemeToggle` calls `applyTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts`\n2. The attribute `data-theme` is written first, then `localStorage` (`THEME_STORAGE_KEY`)\n3. `subscribeTheme` observes the attribute with a `MutationObserver`, and reacts to `storage` events and OS `prefers-color-scheme` changes when nothing is stored\n4. `src/hooks/useTheme.ts` exposes the value to React\n\n### Section Navigation Path\n\n1. Desktop `SiteHeader` and mobile `PillNav` call `onNavigate` = `lockTo(id)` (`src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`)\n2. `lockTo` sets `activeId` immediately and suppresses the observer until `scrollend`, a quiet period, a fallback timer, or a cap timer releases it\n3. The single `IntersectionObserver` band (`rootMargin` built from `--nav-h` and `-60%` bottom) updates `activeId` otherwise\n\n### Copy Email Path\n\n1. Hero and Contact call `useCopyEmail` (`src/components/ui/useCopyEmail.ts`)\n2. `copyText` in `src/lib/copy.ts` tries `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, then falls back to a hidden textarea with `document.execCommand('copy')`\n3. Result is announced through a live region and a toast (`src/components/ui/useToast.ts`, `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`)\n\n**State Management:**\n- No global store. State is local to hooks and components, plus React context for motion preference and toasts.\n- Theme truth is the DOM attribute, not React state. React reads it through `readTheme()`.\n- Scroll-spy state is a `useState` plus refs (`prevRef`, `intersectingRef`, `lockedRef`, `releaseLockRef`, `recomputeRef`) inside `useActiveSection`.\n\n## Key Abstractions\n\n**`siteContent` aggregate:**\n- Purpose: One typed object holding all site data\n- Examples: `src/content/index.ts`\n- Pattern: Plain `export const` data, typed by `src/content/schema.ts`. `contacts.ts` uses `as const satisfies readonly ContactLink[]`.\n\n**Animation barrel:**\n- Purpose: Stable public API for animation, the only allowed import path\n- Examples: `src/anim/index.ts` (exports `MotionFeatures`, `MotionPreferenceProvider`, `ThemeThumb`, and others)\n- Pattern: Facade. Consumers import `@/anim`, never `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n\n**Vendored primitives:**\n- Purpose: Copy-in source from motion-primitives, owned by this repo\n- Examples: `src/components/motion-primitives/text-effect.tsx`\n- Pattern: Source ownership. Edited in place, not installed from npm. Lint rules are turned off for this directory (`.oxlintrc.json` override).\n\n**Scroll-spy hook:**\n- Purpose: Determine the active section and manage click-lock\n- Examples: `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts` (pure helper `pickActive` is exported for unit tests in `tests/unit/active-section.test.ts`)\n- Pattern: IntersectionObserver with a computed band, plus timers for lock release\n\n**Toast and copy:**\n- Purpose: Transient feedback after copying the email\n- Examples: `src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`, `src/components/ui/useToast.ts`, `src/components/ui/useCopyEmail.ts`, `src/lib/copy.ts`\n- Pattern: Context provider plus a hook. Live region for screen readers.\n\n**Project dialog:**\n- Purpose: Project detail view\n- Examples: `src/sections/Projects/ProjectDialog.tsx`\n- Pattern: Native `<dialog>` with `showModal()` called in an effect (ADR-0006 native path, referenced in the file's comments)\n\n## Entry Points\n\n**Application:**\n- Location: `src/main.tsx`\n- Triggers: Browser loads `index.html` (dev server or built `dist/index.html`)\n- Responsibilities: Font import, global CSS import, root render in `StrictMode`\n\n**Not-found page:**\n- Location: `404.html` (second Rollup input in `vite.config.ts`). Styled by `src/styles/not-found.css`.\n- Triggers: GitHub Pages serves it for unknown paths\n- Responsibilities: Static fallback page\n\n**Build and check entries:**\n- Location: `vite.config.ts`, `scripts/*.mjs`\n- Triggers: `npm run build`, `npm run verify`, CI workflows\n- Responsibilities: bundling, asset checks, budget and policy checks\n\n## Architectural Constraints\n\n- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser main thread. No Web Workers in `src/`.\n- **Global state:** `src/lib/theme.ts` holds a module-level `unsavedChoice` flag. `html[data-theme]` is global DOM state. `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts` holds scroll and timer state per hook instance.\n- **Circular imports:** None observed during exploration.\n- **Import boundaries (enforced by oxlint `no-restricted-imports` in `.oxlintrc.json`):**\n  - `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`, `framer-motion`, `motion`, `react-spring` are allowed only in `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/`\n  - Animation must be imported through `@/anim` barrel only\n  - `src/content` may be imported only by `src/app/Page.tsx`\n  - `src/anim/**` must not import `@/sections`, `@/layout`, or `@/content`\n  - `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` checks these rules against fixtures in `tests/fixtures/`\n- **Reduced motion:** Honored through `src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts` and `MotionPreferenceProvider`. Respect this in any new animation.\n- **Static output only:** No runtime server. Any dynamic behavior must run in the browser.\n- **Base path:** Asset URLs must go through `import.meta.env.BASE_URL` or Vite imports, because `VITE_BASE` changes the base.\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Importing motion libraries directly in a section or layout component\n\n**What happens:** A component imports from `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n**Why it's wrong:** Lint fails (`no-restricted-imports`), and the `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` contract breaks. It also bypasses the lazy feature bundle and reduced-motion handling.\n**Do this instead:** Import from `@/anim` (`src/anim/index.ts`). Add a new export to the barrel if a new primitive is needed.\n\n### Importing content from components\n\n**What happens:** A section or layout file imports `@/content` or `src/content/*` directly to read data.\n**Why it's wrong:** Lint restricts content imports to `src/app/Page.tsx`. Data flow goes top-down from `Page`.\n**Do this instead:** Read data in `src/app/Page.tsx` and pass it as typed props, as `Hero`, `Experience`, `Projects`, and others already do.\n\n### Writing theme state into React state only\n\n**What happens:** Setting theme in component state without writing `html[data-theme]`.\n**Why it's wrong:** The inline bootstrap in `index.html` and `subscribeTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts` both treat the DOM attribute as the source of truth. The two can diverge.\n**Do this instead:** Call `applyTheme` in `src/lib/theme.ts` and read with `readTheme`.\n\n### Importing `@/anim/features` statically\n\n**What happens:** A file imports `src/anim/features.ts` directly, pulling `domMax` into the initial graph.\n**Why it's wrong:** The file exists to keep the motion feature bundle in its own chunk, loaded after first paint (`src/anim/features.ts` header comment).\n**Do this instead:** Use `MotionFeatures` from `src/anim/MotionFeatures.tsx`, which loads the feature bundle through `LazyMotion`.\n\n## Error Handling\n\n**Strategy:** Defensive try/catch around browser APIs that can be blocked or missing. Degrade quietly rather than throw.\n\n**Patterns:**\n- `localStorage` access wrapped in try/catch in `src/lib/theme.ts` and `index.html`. The in-memory choice still applies when storage is blocked.\n- `matchMedia` wrapped in try/catch in `src/lib/theme.ts`. Falls back to `light`.\n- Clipboard write falls back from `navigator.clipboard.writeText` to `document.execCommand('copy')` in `src/lib/copy.ts`.\n- `useActiveSection` does nothing when `IntersectionObserver` is missing. `activeId` stays `null`.\n- Scroll lock has fallback and cap timers so a stuck scroll cannot freeze the indicator.\n- `TextReveal` wraps a lazy import in an error boundary class component (`src/anim/declarative/TextReveal.tsx`).\n\n## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n\n**Logging:** None. No logging library. Console output is not a designed channel.\n**Validation:** Compile-time only, via TypeScript types in `src/content/schema.ts` and `satisfies` checks. No runtime validation library.\n**Authentication:** Not applicable (public static site).\n**Accessibility:** Skip link (`src/layout/SkipLink.tsx`), `aria-labelledby` on sections, live region for copy feedback, `prefers-reduced-motion` honored, tests use `axe-core`.\n**Build-time checks:** `scripts/check-*.mjs` enforce path case, color tokens, contrast pairs, JS budget, absence of phone numbers, and image outputs. These run in `npm run verify`.\n\n---\n\n*Architecture analysis: 2026-11-19*\n","numLines":299,"startLine":1,"totalLines":299}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_015xrNauXpQ2zQUnSjQVcJDy","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

<action>\n123\tAll four files live in the phase directory per D-01; wireframes are ASCII/markdown per D-02. This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n124\t\n125\t(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n126\t- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n127\t- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n128\t- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n129\t\n130\t(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n\n(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n\n(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". One format is used for every date on the site and in this file.\n\n1. Month names are written in full: January, February, and so on. No abbreviations, no numeric months.\n2. A single date is `Month YYYY`, for example `July 2026`.\n3. A range is `Month YYYY – Month YYYY`: an en dash (U+2013) with one space on each side, and the year written on both sides, for example `May 2025 – August 2025`.\n4. Resume abbreviations are expanded. The resume's `Aug. 2022` becomes `August 2022`.\n5. Legacy hyphen ranges and short months are normalized. The legacy `June 2023 - Aug 2023` becomes `June 2023 – August 2023`.\n6. Academic-term labels (Spring 2024, Fall 2023, Summer 2022) are converted to month ranges per the G-08 ruling. The original label is kept in the item's Legacy-site value.\n7. This policy is applied to every date in the file. The `Dates` line of each dated item contains only the normalized date, nothing else.\n\n## Hero {#hero}\n\nWireframes: `### Frame: Hero` in `01-IA-WIREFRAMES.md`. When a design or content choice is unclear, this file decides.\n\n## Purpose\n\nA remake of Aaron Phan's personal portfolio, currently the click-wheel iPod site, as a playful, tactile React site with a strong visual identity. The iPod concept is dropped entirely; the new site has its own identity. The content stays the same (same six sections, existing copy and images, updated from the current resume) and the presentation is new.\n\n## Audience\n\nRecruiters and hiring managers, and the design-engineering community, served equally. Recruiters need name, role, experience, projects, resume and contact fast. The design-engineering audience looks for craft in how the page feels. The site has to satisfy both without making either wait.\n\n## Core value\n\nThe site must feel crafted and memorable (tactile, physics-based motion and strong visual identity) while key info stays instantly accessible, on mobile as much as desktop.\n\n## Personality\n\nPlayful, tactile, crafted, plus four more.\n\n- **Playful:** small surprises reward curiosity (a role line that cycles, a copy-email toast that eases in) without blocking anything.\n- **Tactile:** buttons and cards press and squish, the project rail is something you handle, and motion carries weight and settles like a physical object.\n- **Crafted:** consistent spacing, type and motion tokens; nothing looks defaulted; details such as focus rings and reduced-motion states are designed, not patched.\n- **Warm:** soft shapes, large friendly type and gentle color bands, taken from the tone reference.\n- **Confident:** short, plain copy that states what Aaron does and has built, with no filler.\n- **Fast:** pages load quickly on a phone and every interaction responds immediately.\n- **Inclusive:** keyboard, screen reader and reduced-motion users get the same content and the same personality in a calmer form.\n\n## Anti-goals\n\n- Scroll-jacking: the page scrolls natively on touch and never traps the wheel.\n- A preloader or intro animation that blocks content.\n- Hover-only content: everything reachable by hover is also reachable by tap and keyboard.\n- A site-wide custom cursor.\n- 3D or WebGL.\n- Skill percentage bars.\n- Effects stacked on every card: one spatial idea, used where it earns its place.\n- The phone number anywhere.\n\n## The 10-second test\n\nA first-time visitor on a phone can find name, role, experience, projects, resume and contact within 10 seconds.\n\n| Item | Where it lives | How it is reached |\n|------|----------------|-------------------|\n| Name | {#hero} | Visible on first paint with no scrolling |\n| Role | {#hero} | The role line directly under the name |\n| Experience | {#experience} | Bottom pill nav: the Experience segment, one tap |\n| Projects | {#projects} | Bottom pill nav: the Projects segment, one tap |\n| Resume | {#hero} | The hero Resume CTA, one tap |\n| Contact | {#contact} | Hero Contact CTA, one tap (also in the pill Menu panel) |\n\nPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled.\n\n## References\n\nSource clips are in `references/` (private, not in the public repo). Notes come from still frames, so timing and physics are inferred; the feel is verified with the user during the interaction work.\n\n### 539 — Handled project rail (signature)\n\nThe signature interaction: an object you handle. On hover a project lifts out and enlarges while its neighbors shift aside; a click opens a focused detail view with the rail blurred behind it, prev and next controls, an index and a close control. On touch the visitor swipes the rail and taps to open.\n\n- Borrow: the lift, the neighbors making room, the focused detail with a blurred backdrop, prev/next with an index, and a clear close control.\n- Do not borrow: hover as the only way in (touch uses swipe and tap), the garment-and-hanger metaphor, the newsletter ticker, and the corner-only About/Contact placement.\n\n### 445 — Morphing pill nav (mobile)\n\nA bottom pill expands in place into frosted panels, then collapses. One element morphs between states, which is the strongest mobile pattern in the set.\n\n- Borrow: the single pill that expands and collapses in place, the frosted panel surface, and the one-element-morphs idea.\n- Do not borrow: the audiobook-specific panels (search, settings) and the phone-mockup framing.\n\n### 355 — Tone\n\nA soft marketing site with a pastel hero, cream and navy alternating bands, a card carousel, an accordion list and an oversized wordmark footer. It is the tone reference, not the signature.\n\n- Borrow: softness, large type, and alternating background bands between sections.\n- Do not borrow: the cursor-reactive text distortion (hover-only and a site-wide cursor effect), the illustration set, and the cloud-textured wordmark.\n\n### godly.design — Mood board\n\nCurated posts of interface interaction clips. Inspiration only; it is not a dependency and has no code or package implications.\n\n- Borrow: spring feel, press states and motion patterns, captured as written notes in the motion spec before any coding.\n- Do not borrow: whole layouts, or any effect that needs a mouse.\n\n## Launch gates\n\n- Mobile Lighthouse performance at least 90 and accessibility at least 95.\n- Initial JavaScript at most 150 kB gzipped (relaxed from a stricter 120 kB because the stack probe measured about 139 kB before real content; code-split to stay under).\n- LCP at most 2.5 s and CLS under 0.1.\n- WCAG 2.2 AA.\n- Full `prefers-reduced-motion` support.\n\n## Content principles\n\n- The resume PDF is the source of truth; on any conflict it wins over the old site. Items the resume does not cover are kept from the old site.\n- The same six sections as before: About Me, Skills, Education, Experience, Projects, Contact Me.\n- The phone number is never published, in site copy, the served resume, meta tags, JSON-LD or Open Graph data. The served resume is a phone-stripped copy.\n- Public email, GPA and the DJ Instagram link stay public (D-11).\n","numLines":103,"startLine":1,"totalLines":103}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01PZcnshgwubrqDXXwkKuo4u","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n10\t\n11\t## Format\n12\t\n13\tTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n14\t\n15\t- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n16\t- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n17\t- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n18\t\n19\tA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n20\t\n21\tVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n22\t\n23\tRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. B and C override it inside their palette blocks. `--on-primary` and `--on-accent` are the page background in both themes (a light label on the deep light fills, a dark label on the lifted dark fills). `--primary-hover` is the primary pulled slightly toward the text color in light and toward the background in dark (mixing a lifted dark primary toward near-white leaves the gamut), so the button always reads as pressed in. `--focus-ring` is the text color in both themes: it is the only color that holds 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary at once, once the light primary sits in the band described under candidate A.\n116\t\n117\t```derived\n118\tlight --surface mix(--secondary 30%, --background)\n119\tdark --surface mix(--secondary 60%, --background)\n120\tlight --muted mix(--text 70%, --background)\n121\tdark --muted mix(--text 72%, --background)\n122\tlight --border mix(--text 14%, --background)\n123\tdark --border mix(--text 16%, --background)\n124\tlight --border-strong mix(--text 55%, --background)\n125\tdark --border-strong mix(--text 55%, --background)\n126\tlight --link mix(--primary 80%, --text)\n127\tdark --link mix(--accent 100%, --background)\n128\tlight --on-primary mix(--background 100%, --text)\n129\tdark --on-primary mix(--background 100%, --text)\n130\tlight --on-accent mix(--background 100%, --text)\n131\tdark --on-accent mix(--background 100%, --text)\n132\tlight --primary-hover mix(--primary 85%, --text)\n133\tdark --primary-hover mix(--primary 94%, --background)\n134\tlight --focus-ring mix(--text 100%, --background)\n135\tdark --focus-ring mix(--text 100%, --background)\n136\t```\n137\t\n138\t## Candidate B — Clay and cream\n139\t\n140\tNot chosen.\n141\t\n142\tWarm clay on cream. It carries no contrast requirement and is never the only cue for a control boundary; controls use `--border-strong` (3:1).\n356\t- Disabled controls are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, but they still get a non-color cue (reduced weight plus a \"not available\" affordance such as a dashed outline), not color alone.\n357\t- `--secondary` is a fill. It is never used as text or as a lone border.\n358\t\n359\t## Chosen system\n360\t\n361\tCandidate D, neutral grounds with the tuned seed indigo as signal (Phase 3, D-02; the Phase 1 pick was candidate A, which stays recorded above). Plan 01-04 added candidates B and C, the full 19-pair list for every section, the type pairing per candidate, and, after the user picked candidate A (tuned seed indigo, Inter only), the chosen system below.\n\nOwner decisions this file records: D-04 (three candidates, per-theme tokens, the user picks one), D-05 (type explored with color), D-06 (exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints). WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n\n## Format\n\nTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n\n- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n\nA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n\nVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n\nRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n\n## Role tokens\n\nThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. Per-theme values are mandatory (D-04): the seed indigo `2f27ce` measures 2.23:1 on the dark background `050315`, which fails text, UI and focus use.\n\n| Order | Token | Job |\n|-------|-------|-----|\n| 1 | `--text` | Body and heading text, and the on-color for filled dark surfaces |\n| 2 | `--background` | Page background |\n| 3 | `--primary` | Filled buttons, the main brand fill |\n| 4 | `--secondary` | Tint family for cards and soft fills (decorative, never text or a border on its own: `dedcff` on the light background is 1.29:1) |\n| 5 | `--accent` | Highlights and large display color |\n\nDerived tokens (D-06), all `mix()` of roles, defined once for every candidate in the shared `derived` block:\n\n| Token | Job |\n|-------|-----|\n| `--surface` | Card, toast and overlay panel fill |\n| `--muted` | Dates, captions and secondary copy |\n| `--border` | Decorative hairlines (no contrast requirement) |\n| `--border-strong` | Control boundaries (3:1) |\n| `--link` | Inline link text |\n| `--on-primary` | Label on a filled primary button |\n| `--on-accent` | Label on an accent chip or active pill |\n| `--primary-hover` | Hovered or pressed filled button |\n| `--focus-ring` | Keyboard focus indicator |\n\n## Candidate A — Tuned seed indigo\n\nChosen in Phase 1; superseded by candidate D in Phase 3 (D-02). Kept here as the recorded fallback.\n\nContinuity with the realtimecolors seed (050315 / fbfbfe / 2f27ce / dedcff / 433bff). Dark roles are authored for dark, not inverted: the text and background swap ends, primary and accent lift to the 5.66:1 and 8.19:1 class on `050315`, and secondary becomes a dark indigo tint. One tune from the seed in light: `--primary` moves from `2f27ce` to `5046e5` (plan 01-01 had first tuned it to `281fb4`; the full 19-pair set forces a second move). Reason: a focus ring must hold 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary button. With `281fb4` no ring color does all four: a mid-tone ring clears the button but gives 2.50:1 on the secondary tint, and a near-black ring gives 1.89:1 on the button. A primary lighter than the seed's (relative luminance about 0.11 to 0.18) opens the band: a near-black ring then reads on the button (3.2:1 or better) and on every light surface, while the white label on the button still holds 4.5:1. Cost: primary `5046e5` and accent `433bff` are now close in light, so color alone never separates them (Pitfall 5); state uses shape and weight too.\n\nType pairing: Inter variable for display and body, one family: `@fontsource-variable/inter` 5.3.0. Bricolage Grotesque is a variable grotesque with quirky, slightly condensed shapes and an optical size axis, characterful at display size and still clean for short headings.\n\nSwatches (hex of the OKLCH roles below, for reference):\n\n| Role | Light | Dark |\n|------|-------|------|\n| --text | #04211f | #effaf7 |\n| --background | #f3fbf9 | #04191a |\n| --primary | #0f766e | #0b9e91 |\n| --secondary | #c9efe6 | #0c3a3a |\n| --accent | #b45309 | #f0b050 |\n\n```palette C\nlight --text oklch(0.2255 0.0347 188.59)\nlight --background oklch(0.9815 0.0088 179.61)\nlight --primary oklch(0.5109 0.0860 186.39)\nlight --secondary oklch(0.9226 0.0412 179.41)\nlight --accent oklch(0.5553 0.1455 49.00)\ndark --text oklch(0.9761 0.0122 178.03)\ndark --background oklch(0.1965 0.0277 199.29)\ndark --primary oklch(0.6300 0.1100 184)\ndark --secondary oklch(0.3187 0.0478 195.02)\ndark --accent oklch(0.7997 0.1339 74.64)\ndark --link mix(--primary 75%, --text)\n```\n\nDerived overrides: dark `--link` follows the lifted primary (`mix(--primary 75%, --text)`) instead of the accent, so links stay teal in both themes. Teal with an amber accent is lively without being loud, and the contrast between cool fields and a warm accent gives the page a clear second voice for highlights, scroll-spy and active pills. Teal is a common design-engineer choice, so identity depends more on motion and layout than on color.\n\nContrast results:\n\n| Pair | Category | Light | Dark |\n|------|----------|-------|------|\n| --text on --background | text | 16.08 | 16.98 |\n| --text on --surface | text | 15.29 | 13.98 |\n| --text on --secondary | text | 13.66 | 11.71 |\n| --muted on --background | text | 6.91 | 8.42 |\n| --muted on --surface | text | 6.57 | 6.93 |\n| --link on --background | text | 6.66 | 7.48 |\n| --link on --surface | text | 6.34 | 6.16 |\n| --on-primary on --primary | text | 5.21 | 5.45 |\n| --on-primary on --primary-hover | text | 6.30 | 4.89 |\n| --on-accent on --accent | text | 4.78 | 9.52 |\n| --border-strong on --background | ui | 4.26 | 5.14 |\n| --border-strong on --surface | ui | 4.05 | 4.23 |\n| --primary on --background | ui | 5.21 | 5.45 |\n| --accent on --background | ui | 4.78 | 9.52 |\n| --accent on --surface | ui | 4.54 | 7.83 |\n| --focus-ring on --background | focus | 16.08 | 16.98 |\n| --focus-ring on --surface | focus | 15.29 | 13.98 |\n| --focus-ring on --primary | focus | 3.09 | 3.12 |\n| --focus-ring on --secondary | focus | 13.66 | 11.71 |\n\n## Candidate D — Neutral grounds, indigo as signal\n\nChosen (Phase 3, D-02). It carries no contrast requirement and is never the only cue for a control boundary; controls use `--border-strong` (3:1).\n- Disabled controls are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, but they still get a non-color cue (reduced weight plus a \"not available\" affordance such as a dashed outline), not color alone.\n- `--secondary` is a fill. It is never used as text or as a lone border.\n\n## Chosen system\n\nCandidate D, neutral grounds with the tuned seed indigo as signal (Phase 3, D-02; the Phase 1 pick was candidate A, which stays recorded above). Each step carries `--line-height`, `--letter-spacing` and `--font-weight` modifiers, so one utility class (for example `text-xl`) sets all four.\n\n| Token | Size | Line height | Tracking | Weight | Use |\n|-------|------|-------------|----------|--------|-----|\n| `--text-mega` | `var(--t-mega)`, below 768 px `clamp(3.75rem, 0.9rem + 22vw, 6.75rem)`, at 768 px and up `clamp(3.75rem, 0.9rem + 12.2vw, 12rem)` | 0.86 | -0.045em | 800 | Hero h1 poster name |\n| `--text-xl` | `clamp(2.5rem, 1.4rem + 4.8vw, 5.5rem)` | 0.95 | -0.03em | 750 | Section h2 |\n| `--text-l` | `clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.4vw, 2.5rem)` | 1.15 | -0.015em | 500 | Role line, lead paragraphs |\n| `--text-m` | `clamp(1.2rem, 1.1rem + 0.4vw, 1.45rem)` | 1.35 | -0.005em | 600 | Card titles, nav wordmark |\n| `--text-body` | `clamp(1rem, 0.96rem + 0.2vw, 1.0625rem)` | 1.55 | 0 | 400 | Body copy |\n| `--text-s` | 0.875rem | 1.45 | 0.005em | 500 | Dates, card metadata, nav labels |\n| `--text-xs` | 0.8125rem | 1.4 | 0.01em | 500 | Captions, chip labels (never below this) |\n\n`--t-mega` is a custom property set on `:root` in `base.css`, with the 768 px media step there (never in `tokens.css`, which stays flat). Minimum touch target 44 by 44 px (`size-11`) for interactive controls.\n- Radius (Phase 3, D-06, hold versus press): held things are 4 px (`--radius-hold`, utility `rounded-hold`); pressed things are 9999 px (`--radius-pill`, `rounded-pill`); the one declared exception is the expanded pill panel at 28 px (`--radius-panel`, `rounded-panel`). `--radius-sm`, `--radius-md` and `--radius-lg` are deleted. `cn()` teaches tailwind-merge the custom size and radius utility names so they merge correctly.\n- Elevation (per theme, set on `:root` and `[data-theme=dark]`; shadows are decorative, so they carry no contrast requirement; edges that matter use `--border` or `--border-strong`):\n\n| Token | Light | Dark |\n|-------|-------|------|\n| `--shadow-sm` | `0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 10%, transparent)` | `0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.5)` |\n| `--shadow-md` | `0 4px 12px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 12%, transparent)` | `0 4px 12px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.55)` |\n| `--shadow-lg` | `0 12px 32px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 16%, transparent)` | `0 12px 32px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.65)` |\n\n- z-index layers (`--z-*`): base 0, rail-lift 10, sticky-nav 40, pill-nav 50, overlay-backdrop 60, overlay 70, toast 80, skip-link 90. The skip link is the top layer so it is never covered when it takes focus.\n- Breakpoints (mobile first, min-width): 375 baseline (design target, no media query), `md` 768 (`48rem`), `lg` 1024 (`64rem`), `xl` 1280 (`80rem`). These match the Tailwind v4 defaults for md, lg and xl, so no override is needed beyond documenting 375 as the smallest supported width.\n\n## Tailwind v4 mapping\n\n- Theme switch: `html` carries a `data-theme` attribute (`light` or `dark`), set by an inline script in `<head>` before first paint. `color-scheme` is set per theme.\n- Dark variant: `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *));`\n- Role and derived tokens live as plain CSS variables in `tokens.css`: ten role values per theme (the single edit block) and nine derived tokens written as `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`, matching the `mix()` formulas in the Chosen system table. Roles are authored in OKLCH.\n- `@theme inline` maps `--color-text`, `--color-background`, `--color-primary`, `--color-secondary`, `--color-accent`, `--color-surface`, `--color-muted`, `--color-border`, `--color-border-strong`, `--color-link`, `--color-on-primary`, `--color-on-accent`, `--color-primary-hover` and `--color-focus-ring` each to `var(--NAME)`, so utilities such as `bg-surface` and `text-muted` follow the active theme with no `dark:` variants in components. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01L5Kcw9rAg6xMohRiHk3uVK","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-0003: GitHub Pages source, staging, cutover and rollback\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tDate: 2026-10-09\n6\t\n7\t## Context\n8\t\n9\tThe current iPod site is served from the `aa-phan.github.io` repository by the legacy \"Deploy from a branch\" Pages source. The live setting was read from the GitHub API on 2026-10-09:\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\tgh api repos/aa-phan/aa-phan.github.io/pages --jq '{build_type, source, html_url}'\n13\t{\"build_type\":\"legacy\",\"html_url\":\"https://aa-phan.github.io/\",\"source\":{\"branch\":\"main\",\"path\":\"/\"}}\n14\t```\n15\t\n16\tSo the live site is published from branch `main`, path `/`, with `build_type` `legacy`. A Vite build cannot be served that way: the new site needs the \"GitHub Actions\" source, which changes how the live URL is published.\n17\t\n18\tThis development repository is not yet on GitHub. The OD-01 gate on pushing it is resolved (see the [ADR log](README.md)).\n19\t\n20\t## Decision\n21\t\n22\t1. The new site is built by GitHub Actions and first deployed as a staging project site of this repository. `VITE_BASE` is set to `/` plus this repository's name plus `/`, so the staging URL is `https://aa-phan.github.io/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/` and CI catches broken sub-path assets before launch.\n23\t2. The cutover is an additive commit on top of the existing `aa-phan.github.io` history. First the iPod site is tagged (`v1-ipod`) and that tag and a matching branch are pushed, so the old site stays recoverable. Then the iPod files are removed and the new site source is added in a normal commit, merged through a pull request.\n24\t3. The Pages source of `aa-phan.github.io` is switched from the legacy branch source to GitHub Actions in the same sitting as the merge, and the deploy workflow is then triggered with `workflow_dispatch` so the new site goes live immediately.\n25\t4. Force-pushing `aa-phan.github.io` is forbidden, for the cutover and for the rollback.\n26\t5. Private planning files and the private reference folder are not copied into `aa-phan.github.io`. Only the source the site needs, the workflow and `docs/` are.\n27\t\n28\tThe step-by-step procedure, the workflow settings and the smoke test are in the [deploy runbook](../deploy-runbook.md).\n29\t\n30\t## Consequences\n31\t\n32\t- The live site and its history stay recoverable at every point: the old site is a tag, the cutover is one revertible commit, and nothing is rewritten.\n33\t- There may be a short window, while the Pages source is switched, in which the live URL returns a 404. This is possible but unverified (open decision OD-05); the switch and the workflow trigger are done back to back to keep it short.\n34\t- Staging on the project URL proves the Actions pipeline, base-path handling and asset paths before the user-site URL is touched.\n35\t- Staging requires pushing this repository to GitHub, which OD-01 no longer blocks.\n36\t\n37\t## Rollback\n38\t\n39\tIf the new site is broken or the switch goes wrong:\n40\t\n41\t1. In the `aa-phan.github.io` repository settings, set the Pages source back to \"Deploy from a branch\", branch `main`, folder `/`.\n42\t2. Revert the cutover commit with `git revert`, or restore the iPod files from the `v1-ipod` tag with a normal commit.\n43\t3. Never force-push.\n44\t\n45\t## Alternatives considered\n46\t\n47\t- Replace the repository history with the new site (force-push). Rejected: it destroys the old site's history and the rollback path.\n48\t- Deploy the new site from a built-output branch instead of Actions. Rejected: it keeps build artifacts in git history and loses the CI gates.\n49\t- Keep the iPod site where it is and serve the new site only from the project URL. As a modal dialog it must:\n\n1. Trap keyboard focus inside the overlay while it is open.\n2. Close on Escape.\n3. Lock background scroll.\n4. Make the background inert, so assistive technology and tab order cannot reach it.\n5. Return focus to the rail item that opened it.\n6. Expose `role=\"dialog\"` with `aria-modal=\"true\"` and a label taken from the project title.\n7. Keep previous, next and close reachable and usable by keyboard.\n\nThe vendored `MorphingDialog` component from motion-primitives gives the morph animation. Its behavior on the seven points above has not been verified.\n\nThe motion spec splits responsibility the same way: motion animates the overlay, and the dialog primitive owns focus, Escape, inert background and scroll lock.\n\n## Decision\n\nMotion owns the overlay animation: `AnimatePresence` plus a shared `layoutId` morph from the rail item's inner card to the overlay panel, with a crossfade for previous and next. The dialog primitive owns everything on the checklist above: focus trap, Escape, inert background, scroll lock and focus return. The two concerns stay separate.\n\nA code spike checks `MorphingDialog` against the seven-point checklist before the rail ships. The spike itself is deferred to the interaction build (Phase 2 or 4) and is not run as part of the documentation work.\n\n- If every point passes, `MorphingDialog` is used as vendored.\n- If any point fails, the overlay uses a native `dialog` element opened with `showModal()`. Top-layer rendering makes the rest of the page inert and the `cancel` event handles Escape. Focus return and scroll lock are handled explicitly in our code. Motion animates only the inner panel; the `layoutId` morph targets that inner panel rendered inside the `dialog` element, not the `dialog` element itself.\n- Radix Dialog is considered only if both of the above fail, because it adds a dependency.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Overlay animation and overlay accessibility are separate concerns, so either primitive works with the same motion spec and the same reduced-motion fallback (instant open and close, no morph).\n- The native fallback costs a little explicit code (focus return, scroll lock) and no new dependency.\n- With the native fallback, the backdrop blur and the morph are applied to elements inside the `dialog`, because the `dialog` element's own box is not what animates.\n- The rail cannot ship until the spike result is recorded.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Adopt `MorphingDialog` without checking it. That trigger has fired: this repository is public, it hosts the staging site through GitHub Pages, and its main branch has carried the planning area and the assistant instruction file since 2026-10-09. The earlier rule and the remote therefore already disagreed. No option removes what is already public without rewriting remote history, which is never done here.\n\nThe owner was offered three choices before the next push: keep the planning area tracked and public, stop tracking it from this push on, or stop tracking it and also drop it from the unpushed local commits.\n\n## Decision\n\nThis ADR reverses, for this development repository only, the ADR-0001 rule that the working documents stay in a private planning area. The planning area and the assistant instruction file stay tracked and public here. The workflow configuration and the state snapshot kept by the planning tool are committed with them, in one dedicated commit before the push. A machine lock file written by the planning tool has no documentation value and is git-ignored.\n\nEvery other ADR-0001 rule still holds and is restated here so that this ADR carries everything that still applies:\n\n- The architecture doc, the ADRs and the deploy runbook live in the top-level `docs/` folder and are written to be published with the site.\n- The reference folder (the source resume and reference videos) never goes into any public repository, and it stays git-ignored in this repo so a broad `git add` cannot stage it.\n- The site repo (`aa-phan.github.io`) receives only the built site at cutover, never the planning area or the reference folder.\n- Every file under `docs/` is self-contained: it never links into a private area, never names a private planning path or decision label, and never contains the phone number.\n- The phone number is never published anywhere. Before every push the history and tree guards in the deploy runbook must print nothing.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Plans, summaries, state snapshots and the assistant instruction file are browsable by anyone, for this phase and every future phase. Nothing pushed can be unpublished.\n- The planning workflow keeps committing its documents, and they are backed up on GitHub.\n- Privacy now rests on the guards rather than on a private area: the phone-number history and tree searches run before each push and print only commit hashes or file names.\n- ADR-0001 is superseded by this ADR. Its file is unchanged apart from its Status line.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Stop tracking the planning area from this push on. Rejected by the owner: the Phase 2 planning commits would still be pushed as history, and the planning documents would lose their remote backup.\n- Stop tracking it and also drop it from the unpushed local commits. Rejected by the owner: it rewrites local commit hashes quoted in summaries and has the same loss of backup, for little privacy gain since copies already public stay public.\n\n## Revisit when\n\nThe development repository and the site repository merge, the owner wants the planning area private again (which would also need a decision about the already-public history), or the planning area gains content that must not be public.\n","numLines":40,"startLine":1,"totalLines":40}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Vz9T6wqYszZpbZoHH4UWsv","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

It is written so the scaffold can be built directly from it. Decisions with a longer rationale live in the [ADR log](adr/README.md).\n6\t\n7\t## Overview\n8\t\n9\tThe site is a static, zero-backend, single-page React app served from GitHub Pages. There is no router, no global store and no data fetching. The architecture comes down to four seams:\n10\t\n11\t1. Typed content: all copy lives in TypeScript modules checked against one schema.\n12\t2. CSS-variable design tokens: five role colors per theme drive every surface.\n13\t3. An internal animation layer: the only place the two animation libraries are imported.\n14\t4. A build and deploy pipeline: Vite build, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages.\n15\t\n16\tEverything else is conventional React composition with props flowing down.\n17\t\n18\t## Layers\n19\t\n20\tDependencies point down only. A layer may import from layers below it, never above.\n21\t\n22\t```text\n23\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n24\t| app/        main.tsx, App.tsx, Providers, Page.tsx                    |\n25\t|             Page.tsx is the ONLY file that imports content data       |\n26\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n27\t| sections/   Hero, About, Experience, Projects, Skills, Education,     |\n28\t|             Contact                      (props in, JSX out)          |\n29\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n30\t| layout/     Container, Section, SiteHeader, PillNav, Footer,          |\n31\t|             SkipLink, Wordmark                                        |\n32\t+----------------------------------------------------------------------+\n33\t| components/ ui/ (CtaLink, Toast, ThemeToggle, icons)                  |\n34\t| flow\n116\t\n117\tBuild time:\n118\t\n119\t```text\n120\tcontent/*.ts --(typed, satisfies)--> app/Page --props--> sections --props--> layout, ui\n121\tassets/*     --(imagetools, hashed imports)--> image fields in content\n122\t```\n123\t\n124\tRuntime, all client-side with no network use beyond same-origin assets:\n125\t\n126\t- Theme: an inline script in the document head reads localStorage, falls back to prefers-color-scheme, and sets the data-theme attribute on the html element before first paint. The theme provider in React only changes the attribute and storage on a user toggle.\n127\t- Motion preference: the OS reduced-motion setting (plus an optional site override) feeds one hook, useMotionPreference, which configures both animation libraries and the wrapper components. See Reduced motion.\n128\t- Scroll-spy: an IntersectionObserver over the section ids drives useActiveSection, which highlights the current section in the navigation.\n129\t- Pointer and touch input drive react-spring values written straight to the DOM, with no React re-render per frame.\n130\t- Project detail: a click or tap sets local state in the Projects section, which opens an overlay with focus handling.\n131\t\n132\tThere is no global state library. Three small contexts exist: theme, motion preference and, optionally, the active section. Everything else is props.\n133\t\n134\t## Content model\n135\t\n136\tAll types live in src/content/schema.ts:\n137\t\n138\t- Profile: name, tagline, bio paragraphs, optional quote, photo (ImageAsset), contacts.\n139\t- ContactLink: kind (email, github, linkedin or instagram), label, href, whether it is external.\n140\t- ExperienceEntry: id, role, org, optional org URL, optional logo, dates (DateRange), location, bullets, optional highlights and stack.\n141\t- Project: id, title, context kind (personal, employer, course or hackathon) with a label, dates, stack, bullets, relatedExperienceId, featured, optional links and image.\n142\t- EducationEntry: id, degree, school, location, dates, gpa, optional track.\n143\t- SkillGroup: id, label, items as a string array.\n144\t- DateRange: ISO start and end (or present) plus a display label in one normalized format.\n145\t- ImageAsset: src, alt, width, height, optional srcset.\n146\t\n147\tRules:\n148\t\n149\t- Content modules use satisfies against the schema so a missing field fails typecheck.\n150\t- Ordering lives in the data (array order or a priority field), never in components.\n151\t- Copy is taken verbatim from the reviewed content inventory; any edit is recorded there with before and after, not made silently in code.\n152\t- The featured flag decides what appears first on mobile, so \"key info in seconds\" is a data decision.\n153\t- Content tests check that ids are unique, related ids resolve, every image has alt text, every external link is https, and dates parse in descending order.\n154\t- A phone number is not a field anywhere in the model, and must never appear in site copy, metadata or the served resume.\n155\t\n156\t## Design tokens\n157\t\n158\t- Exactly five role tokens per theme: text, background, primary, secondary, accent. Light and dark are authored separately, not inverted.\n159\t- Derived tokens (surface, border, muted text, link, focus ring and so on) are computed from the five roles with color-mix(in oklch, ...). A palette swap therefore edits one block and every derived value follows.\n160\t- The theme is selected by the data-theme attribute on the html element.\n161\t- Tailwind v4 is configured CSS-first: a custom dark variant is bound to [data-theme=dark] with @custom-variant, and an @theme inline block maps utilities to the CSS variables. There is no tailwind.config.js.\n162\t- No raw hex values in components. Components use semantic utilities only; a CI check greps for stray hex.\n163\t- A contrast test recomputes every text, UI and focus pair in both themes against WCAG 2.2 AA (4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text and UI) and fails the build on any miss.\n164\t- Spring and duration values that JavaScript needs are mirrored in CSS variables, with src/anim/tokens.ts as the canonical source for springs.\n165\t\n166\t## Animation layer\n167\t\n168\tsrc/anim/index.ts is the only animation import path for the rest of the app. It exposes a handful of semantic components and hooks, not library primitives.\n169\t\n170\t| Interaction class | Owner |\n171\t|-------------------|-------|\n172\t| Mount and unmount, presence, exit animations | motion |\n173\t| Layout and shared-element transitions | motion |\n174\t| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion |\n175\t| Text and number effects, stagger, ready-made motion-primitives prefabs | motion |\n176\t| Velocity-carrying physics: press-squish, rail hover lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring |\n177\t| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail swipe | CSS |\n178\t| Desktop wheel smoothing only | Lenis |\n179\t\n180\tThe rule: one library animates any given element. Never both libraries on one element or one property, and no Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates. If a vendored primitive duplicates a physics wrapper, one implementation is chosen per interaction and the other stays unused.\n181\t\n182\tSpring and duration tokens are defined once in src/anim/tokens.ts, exported in both libraries' formats (motion's stiffness and damping, react-spring's tension and friction), so the two feel like one system. Fine-pointer effects such as tilt, magnetic pull and spotlight are gated by (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine); touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing. Every wrapper reads the motion preference, renders an instant equivalent when reduced, forwards className, and never hides content in its initial CSS state.\n183\t\n184\t## Reduced motion\n185\t\n186\tOne preference source, useMotionPreference, combines the OS prefers-reduced-motion setting with an optional site override and feeds three consumers:\n187\t\n188\t- motion: the provider renders MotionConfig with its reducedMotion setting. This disables transform and layout animation but not opacity or color, so wrappers handle parallax, scroll-linked and autoplay effects explicitly.\n189\t- react-spring: the provider calls Globals.assign({ skipAnimation }) so every spring jumps to its target; the effect cleans up on change.\n190\t- CSS: a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) guard in base.css shortens transitions and animations and keeps scroll behavior native.\n191\t\n192\tContent is visible by default and is never hidden until JavaScript runs. Hidden initial states are applied client-side inside wrappers, and a noscript rule guarantees visibility. Pressed, focused and selected states must read without motion (color, outline, shape). Lenis is off under reduced motion. The provider listens for changes to the media query so a live OS toggle takes effect without a reload.\n193\t\n194\t## Assets\n195\t\n196\t- Images live in src/assets/images/ and are imported as modules (hashed, long-cached). vite-imagetools produces AVIF and WebP variants and srcset with intrinsic width and height to prevent layout shift. Below-the-fold images lazy-load; the hero image is high priority.\n197\t- Fonts are self-hosted through Fontsource (variable, latin subset, font-display swap), at most two families. No third-party font CDN.\n198\t- Brand icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, Instagram, email) and UI glyphs (close, chevrons, download) are inline SVG components under src/components/ui/icons/. No icon package is installed. See ADR-0005 and ADR-0010 in the ADR log.\n199\t- The resume PDF served from public/ is the owner's phone-number-free export of the resume. The phone-number gate reads its text layer, link annotations and metadata, and rejects a stand-in file.\n200\t- Only images that are actually used migrate from the previous site, with EXIF metadata stripped. Template leftovers are left behind.\n201\t\n202\t## Build and deploy\n203\t\n204\tGitHub Actions builds the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages. The Vite base comes from the VITE_BASE environment variable: the project URL path (for example /aa-phan-portfolio-v2/) while staging, and / after the cutover to the user-site URL. Assets are module-imported so no absolute asset paths exist; anything under public/ that JavaScript references goes through import.meta.env.BASE_URL. CI also builds with the project-path base so a broken sub-path is caught before launch. The build has a second HTML entry, 404.html, a static not-found page that GitHub Pages serves for unknown paths. Steps, settings, cutover and rollback are in the deploy runbook (deploy-runbook.md).\n205\t\n206\t## Quality gates\n207\t\n208\t| Gate | Command | Fails the build when
